findings.title: Stray `if` modifier on `end` makes the ERB template invalid or wrong
findings.body: The closing tag `<%- end if %>` is a dangling `if` modifier with no condition. When ERB compiles the template, Ruby either fails with a syntax error or treats the following output code as the modifier's condition. Either way the embed `best` page, which is the main public embed view, breaks or renders incorrectly. The intended closing is a plain `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Remote/feed HTML is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered unsanitized
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, so Post#cook returns the raw string unchanged and nothing sanitizes it. For the RSS path (PollFeed) the content is the feed's `content` field with only CGI.unescapeHTML applied, so any <script> or event-handler markup in the feed is stored verbatim. best.html.erb then outputs it with `raw post.cooked`, which is stored XSS in the embed iframe and in any other place the post is shown. Imported HTML should be sanitized (e.g. with the same tag/attribute whitelist used in import_remote) before it is stored as raw_html.

findings.title: raw_html cook method bypasses the whole cooking and plugin filter pipeline
findings.body: cook returns the raw text for any post whose cook_method is raw_html, skipping both PrettyText sanitization and the Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hook. Combined with PostCreator (lib/post_creator.rb line 216) which accepts opts[:cook_method] from any caller, a code path that forwards user-supplied options to PostCreator could create unsanitized HTML posts. The cook method should be restricted to trusted internal callers, and sanitization should be applied to the raw HTML instead of skipping it.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is set to the full Referer URL, so resize messages are dropped
findings.body: postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme, host, port). Passing request.referer, which is a full URL including path and query, makes the browser fail to match the parent window, so the discourse-resize message is silently not delivered and the iframe never grows. Also, the value is injected into a JavaScript string with ERB output, which is fragile. The origin should be computed from the referer, or '*' should be avoided and the parent origin validated explicitly.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring matching instead of exact origin comparison
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` treats any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl as trusted. This is a loose check that should be an exact comparison of e.origin against the origin parsed from discourseUrl. Messages from unintended origins can then drive the iframe height. The e.data.height value is also used unvalidated in `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"`.

findings.title: Behavior change: update_post now validates per opts but is also used by import paths without guard
findings.body: The change from @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) is fine on its own, but PostRevisor.revise! with skip_validations is now used by TopicEmbed.import on the update path with bypass_rate_limiter. A failed save here is ignored: update_post does not check the return value, and TopicEmbed.import then calls embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) anyway. The stored content hash then records a revision that was never saved, so future imports will not retry the update.

findings.title: Feed item without content raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire poll
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` is called unconditionally. Feed entries that only have a summary, or no body, return nil for content and raise NoMethodError. Because this runs inside rss.items.each, one such item stops the import of every later item in the feed, and the hourly job fails each time. The nil case should be handled (fall back to summary or skip the item).

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string with `<<`
findings.body: `contents << ...` modifies the string passed in by the caller. PollFeed passes content from a parsed feed and import_remote passes doc.content, so the caller's object is changed. Calling import twice with the same string appends the footer twice, and the content hash for the second call changes. The footer should be added to a new string (e.g. `contents = contents + ...`).

findings.title: Concurrent imports of the same URL can create duplicate topics or raise RecordNotUnique
findings.body: The check `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by creating a topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!` is not protected by a lock. Two concurrent imports (e.g. retrieve_topic jobs for the same URL from different anonymous visitors, or PollFeed overlapping with a retrieve job) both see no embed and both create a post. One then fails the unique index on embed_url with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, causing the job to error, and the transaction rolls back the post. The import should handle that exception or use a lock keyed on the URL.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options value ALLOWALL is not a valid header value
findings.body: The only valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM <uri>. Browsers ignore unknown values, so the header does not express the intended policy. Framing permission should be expressed via a Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive that lists the embeddable host, or the header should be removed deliberately with a comment explaining the choice.

findings.title: create_table with force: true silently drops an existing table and its data
findings.body: If the topic_embeds table already exists when this migration runs, force: true drops it and every existing embed mapping is lost. Each lost mapping means the next request for that URL creates a duplicate topic. A migration should not drop tables. Plain create_table without force is the safe choice.

findings.title: Edited an already-shipped migration to add force: true
findings.body: Adding force: true to an existing migration changes its behavior on any database where it has not run yet, and it will drop any top_topics table that exists at that time. Changing a migration that may have been run in another environment is risky. A new migration should be used for any schema correction.

findings.title: Removed the --category option without replacement and changed import semantics
findings.body: The disqus import command's `--category` option is removed silently. Users who pass -c now get a Thor error. The import also switches from creating topics directly to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which downloads each thread's link and creates a topic from the page, not from the Disqus data. Rerunning the import now appends comments to existing embed topics. The behavior change needs to be documented, and the removed option needs a replacement or a deprecation message.

findings.title: Test named 'is 404' asserts only not-success and runs before the guard that actually fails
findings.body: The example 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not check for a 404. Without stubs, the before_filter ensure_embeddable raises first because embeddable_host is blank, so the test passes for an unrelated reason. The missing-parameter path (params.require) is never exercised. The test should stub the host and referer and assert the status that the missing parameter actually produces.

findings.title: No test covers the feed import logic in poll_feed
findings.body: The spec only checks that poll_feed is delegated to when the settings are present. The actual item handling (URL fallback to id, nil content, the import call) is untested, which is why the nil-content crash in poll_feed goes unnoticed. Tests should cover items with missing content and invalid links.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder and does not explain the feature
findings.body: The description reads 'Test 4', so reviewers have no information on the embed feature, the new feed polling and remote import behavior, the new raw_html cook method, or the disqus import change. The description should summarize these and the security implications of importing HTML.
